page.layout: One printed page: running text in one column, a narrow column of marginal note at the right edge; running head at top; catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: ternis excalefactis, temperat ipsos frigore convenienti. Hinc refrigeratio contingit, & purificatio: Unde à Cicerone aer dicitur anima. Ad cordis igitur & aliorum éstuantium membrorum temperandum calorem conducit; Ad respirationem pulmonum, ad corporis mobilitatem facit, adfert enim tenuitatem, ne legnitie torpeant; Adfert itèm corporibus raritatem.
Ab aëre non corrupto conservatur aqua. Aër quoque est visionis medium.
Aër quò purior & tenuior fuerit, eò quoque nobis salubrior; quò impurior, eò perniciosior.
Purus autem aër an alicubi invenia-tur, dubitant Peripatetici, ob Elementorum & aliorum corporum mutuam inter se conjunctionem : unde impuritas quædam contrahitur.An purus aër inveniatur;

Crassus igitur exiftit aër è commixtione Ignis, aquæ, & terræ. Insalubris aër est, qui montibus inclusus non diffatur, & qui animalium, olerum, aut leguminum putredine, aut fimo coinquinatur. Insalubris quoqi nimis humidus,

page.notes: The catchword "qui" is printed at the foot right. The marginal note "An purus aër inveniatur;" is in small italic at the right margin beside the paragraph "Purus autem". The text "éstuantium" and "legnitie", "torpeant;", "itèm" are printed as shown. Some letters at the right and left edges and show-through from the reverse side are faint and left out. The heading-line "Adfert" and "eò" are read from the scan with some uncertainty; the word "legnitie" may be "frigidie" but the scan reads as printed. Possible printing error: "quoqi" for "quoque" at the foot of the page; "qui" at the foot is the catchword.
